---
title: "Understand Hydra configuration"
---

A configuration records the decisions that would otherwise be arguments in a
Python script: the dataset, model architecture, training options and evaluation.
Hydra combines named configurations and applies command-line overrides. METIS
ships those configurations inside the installed package; no source checkout or
editing of library files is required.

## Inspect before changing

```bash
uv run metis train --cfg job
uv run metis train --help
```

The first command prints the fully composed job without training. The second
lists configuration groups. `model=transformer` selects a different model group;
`training.steps=1000` changes one value in the training configuration.

```bash
uv run metis train model=transformer training.steps=1000 model.model_options.n_embd=128
```

The model configuration has this structure:

```yaml
_target_: metis.Surrogate
_convert_: all
model: mlp
observed_outputs: []
model_options:
  hidden_dim: 64
  num_blocks: 2
  num_layers_per_block: 2
```

`_target_` identifies the Python constructor; `_convert_: all` gives it ordinary
Python containers. This is equivalent to constructing `Surrogate("mlp",
model_options={...})`. Width/depth are architecture settings; dimensions derived
from the bank are deliberately not user overrides.

## Your own data and runs

```bash
uv run metis train dataset=parquet dataset.path=/absolute/path/bank.parquet 'dataset.inputs=[contact_rate,recovery_rate]' 'dataset.outputs=[incidence,prevalence]' training.steps=1000
```

Quote list expressions so the shell does not interpret brackets. Relative paths
resolve from the launch directory. See [data preparation](../package/data.qmd)
for column contracts and [the own-bank exercise](../package/own-bank.qmd) for CSV.
The `--multirun` flag expands comma-separated choices into independent jobs:

```bash
uv run metis train --multirun model=mlp,transformer training.learning_rate=0.001,0.0003 evaluation.partition=validation
```

Each job saves its resolved settings with its artifacts. Use validation to select
a run, then assess the selected model on the withheld test bank. `+key=value`
adds a new Hydra key; use it only for a real optional field accepted by its
constructor, not to bypass an unrecognized architecture option.

The [experiment guide](../package/hydra.qmd) covers W&B and custom dataset
factories. More composition details are in the [Hydra tutorials](https://hydra.cc/docs/tutorials/intro/).
The [migration guide](../package/migration.qmd) maps historical configurations
to the installed workflow.
